title: RBI Cracks Down on Bank's "Dark Patterns" and Mis-selling
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued new guidelines to curb unfair sales practices by banks and financial service providers. These guidelines specifical.

faq.a: Dark patterns are deceptive design tactics used in digital interfaces to trick or manipulate customers into making unintended decisions, such as buying extra products or sharing more data, often against their best interests.

faq.q: How do these new RBI guidelines protect me?
faq.a: The guidelines mandate transparency, explicit customer consent, and prohibit forced bundling of products. This means banks cannot trick you into buying products you don't want or need, ensuring your financial decisions are informed.

faq.q: Can my bank still bundle products like a loan and insurance?
faq.a: Banks can *offer* bundled products, but they *must* also offer each component separately. You have the right to choose the primary product without being forced to buy the additional, bundled item.

faq.q: What should I do if I suspect mis-selling?
faq.a: First, raise a complaint with your bank's customer service. If the issue is not resolved to your satisfaction, you can escalate it to the Reserve Bank of India's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, which provides a free and speedy redressal mechanism.

faq.q: Are these rules applicable to all financial institutions?
faq.a: Yes, these "Directions on Fair Practices Code for Lenders" apply to all Regulated Entities (REs) under the RBI's purview, which includes commercial banks, cooperative banks, NBFCs, and other financial service providers.

faq.q: Will these rules make banking slower or more complex?
faq.a: While banks might need to adjust their sales processes, the aim is to make transactions clearer and more ethical, not necessarily slower. The focus is on informed consent, which ultimately benefits the customer.
